subject: Re: Migration PoC - Architecture review / reschedule

From: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-retail.com>

Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Migration PoC - architecture review scheduling

Hi Marissa / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week - the team liked Redwood's latency and the fallback routing idea. We'd like to move forward with the Migration PoC and schedule a deep-dive architecture review with our infra and security folks.

High-level asks for the session:
- Walk through network connectivity options for a Private deployment (VPC peering vs. private link).
- Discuss data flow and audit/logging for inference requests (retention, redaction possibilities).
- Review model migration steps from our current provider (tokenization differences, kv-cache warmup, quantization expectations).
- Confirm timeline for a 2-week PoC, what artifacts you need from us, and a mutual action plan.

Our availability: Tues/Wed next week (May 19-20) between 9am-2pm PT. Let us know which times work and who from your engineering side will join.

I've attached a short requirements doc for the PoC.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
attachments: acme_poc_requirements.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

Hi Elena - thanks for the doc, looks great. Happy to run the architecture review.

We have a 90-minute slot open on Wednesday May 20 at 10:00am PT. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and attach the Redwood network diagram and initial PoC plan. If you prefer Tues, we can do 1:00pm PT.

Thanks - will await confirmation and any additional folks from your side (security/contact).

Thanks all - invite sent for May 20, 10:15-11:45am PT (Google Meet link in invite).

Quick notes responding to Elena's pre-call question about firewall/IPs:
- For Redwood Private we publish a fixed set of egress IP ranges per region; for US those are: 34.217.120.0/22, 52.35.64.0/18 (these are example ranges for pre-approval).
- Standard ports: 443 outbound TLS for API traffic. If you opt for VPC peering, traffic stays on private RFC1918 ranges and you only need to open ports to the internal subnets we agree on.
- We'll provide a detailed IP/port matrix in a follow-up email as an attachment (expected before the call).

Looking forward to the session - we'll record and share slides + the migration checklist afterward.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
